newsitem.title: USA: Interneuron says combined stroke therapy promising.
newsitem.headline: Interneuron says combined stroke therapy promising.

text.p: Interneuron Pharmaceuticals Inc said Thursday that treatment that combined citicoline and Merck and Co Inc's MK-801 was neuroprotective in animal models of stroke, under conditions in which these agents would be ineffective individually.

Interneuron said a previous first Phase III trial showed citicoline alone significantly improved neurologic and cognitive functions in ischemic stroke patients, compared with a placebo. MK-801 is an N-methyl-D-aspartic acid (NMDA) antagonist. It interacts with the receptor complex on neurons.

According the company, NMDA antagonists are believed to be effective only following acute, or short-term administration as soon as possible, while citicoline is believed to have both acute and restorative, or chronic, effects.

Interneuron said this is the first time synergistic benefits have been demonstrated with two drugs meant for different administrations for stroke. The company said that, pending results of a second Phase III trial, it plans to submit a New Drug Application for citicoline for treatment of stroke to the Food and Drug Administration by the end of 1997.
Interneuron obtained exclusive development and commercialization rights to citicoline in the U.S. and Canada from Grupo Ferrer, a Spanish pharmaceutical company, in 1993.
